title: No visual distinction between the "preferred device zero volume" state and the "global mute" state
line: Pressing the Mute key after lowering the volume to 0% now unmutes the speakers at a low volume instead of showing "Audio Muted" again.
explanation: Lowering the volume to 0% mutes the preferred device itself. The Mute key only toggles global mute, which doesn't touch a device it didn't mute, so both presses left the device at 0% and muted and showed the same "Audio Muted" OSD. Now, when global mute is off and the preferred device is both muted and at 0%, the Mute key raises its volume by one step and unmutes it, as the reporter's second option suggested; a device at 0% that isn't muted still gets global mute as before.

commits.message:
kded: Unmute a device at 0% by raising its volume with the Mute key

Lowering the volume to 0 mutes the device, and pressing Mute then only
toggled global mute, which left it muted with the same OSD. If the device
is muted at 0%, the Mute key now raises it by one step and unmutes it.

BUG: 506791

media.caption: Volume down to 0%, then Mute twice: "Audio Muted" all three times
Same steps: the first Mute unmutes at 5%, the second mutes again
Device at 0% but not muted (set elsewhere), Mute: global mute, "Audio Muted"
Same steps: still global mute, the volume is not raised
